subject: Geopolitics
title: Bilateral vs Multilateral Alliances
description: A fast breakdown of Bilateral vs Multilateral Alliances for builders.

hook.text: The US has bilateral deals with Japan, Korea, and Australia. In Europe, it works through 32-member NATO. Why differ?

buildup.text: Bilateral alliances are one-on-one. The US sets terms with each partner. Control is tighter but coordination is harder.

discovery.text: Multilateral alliances share burdens and amplify power. But decisions are slow and free-riding is tempting.

twist.text: Asia's bilateral hub-spoke model worked when the US was dominant.

climax.text: AUKUS and the Quad are bridging the gap — adding multilateral layers to Asia's network for the first time.

punchline.text: One ally is a friendship. Many allies are a system.

quiz.question: Why does Asia primarily have bilateral alliances instead of a NATO equivalent?
options: The US designed a hub-spoke model for tighter control
There was no common military threat in Asia
